question:
Let \([x]\) denote the largest integer (positive, negative or zero) less than or equal to \(x\). Let \(y=f(x)=[x]+\sqrt{x-[x]}\) be defined for all real numbers \(x\).

(i) Sketch on plain paper, the graph of the function \(f(x)\) in the range \(-5\le x\le5\).

(ii) Show that, given any real number \(y_0\), there is a real number \(x_0\), such that \(y_0=f(x_0)\).

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
